project.name: Evidence of Life
project.current_stage: Public open-source project with approximately 30–40 early users

core_positioning.primary_statement: Evidence of Life is an ADHD-friendly visual planning and life-memory system that combines task lists, a draggable daily timeline, planned-versus-actual tracking, and map-based moments.
core_positioning.short_statement: A visual system for turning intended time into lived memory.
core_positioning.product_thesis: Most productivity tools record what people intend to do, while journals record memories after they happen. Evidence of Life connects planning, lived time, photos, places, and memory in one private system.
core_positioning.medical_disclaimer: Designed around challenges commonly experienced by people with ADHD. It is not a diagnostic, clinical, or treatment tool.
core_positioning.recommended_tagline: See where your time went. Remember where life happened.
alternative_taglines: A timeline for where your time went, and a map of where your life happened.
From intended time to lived time.
Plan visually. Live flexibly. Remember spatially.
Turn plans into time, and moments into places.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Time feels abstract and difficult to perceive.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: A person may know what they need to do but cannot clearly see how the work fits into the day.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: A visible timeline externalizes time as concrete blocks.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Show the same tasks as a plain list and then placed into a daily timeline.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Task lists show workload but not feasibility.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: Users create long lists without seeing conflicts, duration, transitions, or available gaps.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: Tasks can be dragged from a list directly into realistic time windows.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Before-and-after comparison of a task list versus a scheduled timeline.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Users may underestimate or overestimate how long activities take.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: A one-hour plan may actually take two hours, causing the rest of the day to collapse.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: Planned-versus-actual views make estimation patterns visible.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Display planned duration beside actual start, end, and elapsed time.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Starting a task can require too much activation energy.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: Users may avoid starting because the task feels too large or the available time feels too small.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: Drag-and-drop scheduling, visible next actions, and short focus sessions lower the cost of starting.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Show a small task dragged into a 15-minute opening and started immediately.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Small time windows are difficult to recognize and use.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: Five, fifteen, or thirty-minute gaps may disappear without meaningful progress.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: The timeline makes available gaps visible and allows appropriately sized tasks to be placed into them.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Highlight an open time gap and drag a short task into it.

adhd_pain_points.user_experience: Rigid planning tools make users rebuild the schedule or feel that the day has failed.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: Tasks can be moved, resized, deferred, or left unfinished without deleting the original intention.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Show a task being moved later while the original plan remains part of the record.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Reconstructing the day from memory requires too much effort.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: At night, users may remember being busy but not what happened, when it happened, or where they were.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: Calendar events, focus sessions, photos, notes, and locations preserve contextual evidence.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Show an automatically assembled recap created from multiple evidence sources.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Activities are spread across separate tools.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: Tasks, calendars, photos, notes, and locations have no shared context.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: Evidence of Life connects these records through time and place.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Select one activity and show its task, focus time, photo, note, and map location.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Productivity systems often treat unfinished plans as failure.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: Partial work and changed plans disappear or create guilt.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: The product preserves partial progress and deviations as evidence of the real day.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Show a partially completed task and the actual activity recorded without a failure state.

adhd_pain_points.problem: Completed tasks disappear without becoming part of a meaningful personal history.
adhd_pain_points.user_experience: People optimize completion but lose the story of their lives.
adhd_pain_points.product_response: Moments, photos, activities, and places remain visible over time and across the map.
adhd_pain_points.visual_proof: Zoom from a daily moment to a city map and then to a global history.

implementation: No requirement for a perfect completed day
Compare intention with reality without judgment

unique_product_features.value: Users can drag tasks from lists into visible time blocks and rearrange the day without rewriting the plan.
unique_product_features.differentiation: Unlike a traditional list, the interface exposes duration, available time, conflicts, and feasibility.
unique_product_features.recommended_label: Plan visually with drag-and-drop time blocks

unique_product_features.value: Users retain a flexible backlog while planning only the tasks that realistically fit today.
unique_product_features.differentiation: The product does not force users to choose between a task manager and calendar.
unique_product_features.recommended_label: Keep intentions flexible and time concrete

unique_product_features.value: Users can see when work actually started, how long it lasted, and how the day changed.
unique_product_features.differentiation: The system records lived time instead of only completion status.

unique_product_features.value: Photos and moments leave visible traces across neighborhoods, cities, countries, and the globe.
unique_product_features.differentiation: The product organizes memory through both time and space.

unique_product_features.value: Calendar events, focus sessions, moments, photos, and places can help rebuild the story of a day.
unique_product_features.differentiation: Users do not need to write a complete journal entry from a blank page.
unique_product_features.recommended_label: Reconstruct the day from real evidence

unique_product_features.value: Users can privately host and retain their own records.
unique_product_features.differentiation: There is no social feed or pressure to perform life publicly.
unique_product_features.recommended_label: A private record, not a social feed

map_positioning.current_problem: A standard map with pins can appear decorative or similar to ordinary travel tracking.
map_positioning.desired_positioning: The map should be presented as a spatial memory layer and a record of lived context.
map_positioning.core_statement: Memories do not live only in dates. They also live in places.
user_value: Photos and moments become easier to remember through location cues.
Users can see traces across a city and eventually across the globe.
Places can reveal patterns in focus, activity, mood, and routines.
A city becomes a visual record of lived experience rather than a collection of anonymous pins.

recommended_visual_states.content: Detailed moments, photos, cafés, campus locations, parks, or workspaces.
Clusters showing where daily life is concentrated.
Cities and countries connected through long-term personal traces.
Photo, date, note, linked activity, time spent, and related memories.

avoid: Do not describe the map only as visited places.
Do not imply constant surveillance or automatic tracking unless the feature actually supports it.
Do not present the map as an ADHD treatment feature.
Do not use real personal location data in the public demo.

readme_plan.early_validation_copy: Evidence of Life has been tested by approximately 30–40 early users. The product has evolved through direct, informal feedback, especially around visual timeline planning, drag-and-drop scheduling, lower-friction capture, reminders, understanding where time goes, and map-based memory. Earlier feedback was not consistently archived as public issues, so these themes are presented as a qualitative summary rather than formal research metrics.
avoid: Do not lead with a long badge row before explaining the product.
Do not describe the project as only a full-stack life management platform.
Do not bury the timeline and map below a generic feature list.
Do not make unverified medical or clinical claims.
Do not invent retention, active-user, or self-hosting statistics.
Do not use real personal photos or location history in public screenshots.

final_message_hierarchy: Evidence of Life helps people see where their time went.
Task lists remain flexible while the timeline makes plans concrete.
Drag-and-drop planning lowers the friction of building and changing a day.
Planned-versus-actual records preserve reality instead of only completed tasks.
Photos and moments leave meaningful traces across cities and the globe.
The product has evolved through feedback from approximately 30–40 early users.
It is ADHD-friendly by design, but it is not a diagnostic or treatment tool.
It is private, open source, self-hostable, and actively maintained.
